Both portraits use identical visible characters. In the encoded copy, 908 red-channel values differ from the original by exactly one level. Scrolling is synchronized.

How it works

One hidden bit per colored character

01

Package the message

The custom frame contains SAS1, the message length, the UTF-8 message, and a CRC-32 checksum.

02

Store one bit in each color

Each byte becomes eight bits. Each bit is stored in the least significant bit of one character's red color value.

03

Change as little as possible

When a red value does not already contain the required bit, it changes by only one level out of 255. The visible character itself never changes.

0x86 = 10000110 → last bit = 0 The next character carries the next bit.

The payload is stored in the HTML color values of the ASCII portrait, not in the original JPEG. This is steganography, not encryption.
